procedural_matters: The panel of the International Jury was composed in accordance with RRS N1.4(b).
AUS 224183 was represented by Richard Longbottom.
ESP 221801 did not come to the hearing, the hearing proceeded in accordance with RRS 63.1(b).
ESP 221801 did not come to the hearing when the protest committee gave the decision.
facts: The incident occurred 30 seconds before the start of Race 8.
AUS 224183 entered a gap 2.5 boat lengths to leeward of ESP 221801, slowed almost to a stop, and held her course.
ESP 221801 bore off more than 90 degrees onto a collision course with AUS 224183.
When the bow of ESP 221801 was 1.5 metres away from AUS 224183's hull abeam of the mast, ESP 221801 luffed.

Contact occurred between the port side of ESP 221801 and the starboard side of AUS 224183. The boom of ESP 221801 hit the mast of AUS 224183 and the main sheet became entangled with her wind indicator.
Both boats remained stopped while the mainsheet of ESP 221801 was released from the wind indicator of AUS 224183.
On the hail of protest from AUS 224183, ESP 221801 looked back and made repeated eye contact with AUS 224183.
conclusions: ESP 221801 to windward failed to keep clear of AUS 224183 to leeward, and broke RRS 11.

By knowingly breaking rule 11 and not taking the appropriate penalty, ESP 221801 failed to compete in compliance with the principles of sportsmanship and fair play as stated in RRS Basic Principles. ESP 221801 broke RRS 2.
ESP 221801 did not avoid contact with AUS 224183 even though it was reasonably possible, and broke RRS 14(a).
It was not reasonably possible for AUS 224183 the right-of-way boat to avoid contact with ESP 221801 when it became clear that ESP 221801 was not keeping clear. AUS 224183 did not break RRS 14(a).
